extracted.intended_audience: citizens, state delegates, and policymakers concerned with constitutional design (originally 'the People of the State of New York')
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance for designing the executive branch of a republican government: what qualities, powers, and institutional arrangements produce an 'energetic' yet safe Executive. Focuses on unity, duration, support, powers, dependence on the people, and responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredients of executive energy
rubrics_metrics.description: The ingredients which constitute energy in the Executive are, first, unity; secondly, duration; thirdly, an adequate provision for its support; fourthly, competent powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit four-part checklist for what makes an Executive 'energetic' enough to protect the community, administer laws, protect property, and defend against ambition/faction. Use this set as the baseline when evaluating or designing an executive: ensure the office is unified, lasts long enough to act firmly, has secure support (resources/salary), and holds the powers necessary to perform duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of the Executive
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity — a single Executive — is conducive to energy: 'Decision, activity, secrecy, and despatch will generally characterize the proceedings of one man ...' Unity should not be destroyed by plurality or by an ostensible single magistrate subject to controlling counsellors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a single chief magistrate rather than multiple magistrates or a council that must concur. Unity produces decisiveness and makes the Executive a single object for the public's jealousy and watchfulness. Anti-patterns: dual consuls, multi-member executives, or an executive dependent on a binding council (which cause dissension, delay, weakened authority, and factional splits). Examples cited: problems with Roman consuls, state councils, and the Decemvirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration in office
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient duration in office increases personal firmness and the stability of administration; too short a tenure produces feebleness and irresolution. A term of four years is argued to be a practical compromise to promote firmness without undue danger to liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing term length, evaluate how it affects the executive's independence from sudden popular passions and from legislative influence. Short terms (or immediate re-election uncertainty) incentivize pliancy to prevailing currents; longer terms give the Executive time to establish reputation and act with vigor. Consider empirical trade-offs (e.g., four years recommended as materially beneficial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate provision for the Executive's support
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'adequate provision for its support' is one of the essential ingredients of executive energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Executive's material independence (secure salary/resources) so that it need not be pecuniarily beholden to other branches or factions. Absence of adequate support undermines firmness and leaves the office susceptible to legislative leverage or corruption. (Related anti-pattern: underfunding that forces dependence on legislature.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent executive powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive must possess 'competent powers' — adequate authority to protect the community against foreign attack, administer the laws, protect property, and safeguard liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant the Executive the specific constitutional powers required to perform core responsibilities effectively; undefined or insufficient powers lead to a 'feeble execution' and thus a bad government in practice. Evaluate powers against the duties of defense, administration, finance, and acting in emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due dependence on the people (popular control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety in the republican sense includes 'a due dependence on the people' — the Executive must remain accountable to the electorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design mechanisms (e.g., elections, popular responsiveness) that connect the Executive to public will without forcing unthinking compliance with every transient popular impulse. Balance dependence so the Executive can resist temporary follies while still answering to the people's deliberate sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due responsibility (personal accountability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety also includes 'a due responsibility' — personal responsibility of the magistrate for his behavior in office (both to censure and to punishment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutionalize clear lines of individual accountability (political censure/removal, legal punishment where appropriate). Avoid arrangements that diffuse responsibility (e.g., multi-member executives or binding councils) because they make detection of culpability difficult and allow blame-shifting and plausible pretexts ('I was overruled by my council').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plurality or binding executive councils
rubrics_metrics.description: The plurality of the Executive tends to deprive the people of security: it divides censure, conceals misconduct, invites collusion, increases expense, and weakens administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject or heavily constrain proposals for multi-person executives or councils whose concurrence is necessary. Specific harms to watch for: difficulty of assigning blame, collusion or artful ambiguity among members, scandalous appointments blamed on divided responsibility, increased public expense, and easier combination of interests against liberty (when a small number can be led by an artful leader).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive independence from the legislature (separation of powers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The separation of powers must make each branch independent of the others; the Executive should not be subordinate or dependent on the legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutional barriers so the Executive is not at the legislature's 'absolute devotion' (e.g., avoid mechanisms where legislative influence can remove or coerce the Executive indirectly). Be alert to the legislature's natural tendency to absorb power; ensure term length, tenure security, and appointment powers protect executive independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment authority and administrative stability
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who manage administration (assistants/deputies) should be the Executive's appointees and subject to his superintendence, linking duration of the chief magistrate to stability of administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vest nomination and (where appropriate) appointment authority for executive subordinates in the chief magistrate to ensure coherence and continuity of administration. Recognize that frequent turnover or successor-driven reversals (where successors routinely reverse predecessors) undermines durable policy and administrative stability.
